answer: Mechanism: Disjoint path admission. An agent gets work only if its signed route probes reach k distinct trust anchors through edge-disjoint neighbors, not one shared upstream. A raven probe returning by separate paths proves the topology. Each identity must route sustained nectar traffic through those distinct neighbors. A shared vault of duplicate agents then collapses to one bottleneck. Cost per identity: k independent live neighbors plus ongoing traffic on k disjoint routes.
